message.content:
{"passages":[{"reference":"20.6","text":"When Peter heard these things, he became thoughtful for a little while and said, “I do not think anyone can discuss evil without doing the will of the evil one himself. Consequently, knowing this very thing, I do not know what I shall do—whether I shall remain silent or speak. If I were to remain silent, I would incur ridicule among the multitude, because, though professing to proclaim truth, I am ignorant of the discourse concerning evil. But if I were to speak, I fear that perhaps God is not pleased for evil to be investigated, but only good. Nevertheless, for you too, in response to Saphonius’s argument, I will make my own views clearer.

“I too agree that not everything belonging to human beings should be attributed to God. For example, human beings, since they do not have bodies capable of transformation, do not transform themselves, but by nature are altered over time through changes. God, however, is not like this, for through his innate spirit and by an ineffable power, the body becomes whatever kind he wishes. And this is more readily believable than even that the air, having received such a nature from him, is transformed into dew by the incorporeal mind that permeates it and, when condensed, becomes water; that water, when solidified, becomes stones and earth; and that stones, when struck together, kindle fire. To such an extent, through alteration and transformation, the air, after first becoming water, ended in fire through these transformations, and what was wet was changed into the opposite nature.

“What then? Did God not also transform Moses’s staff into a living creature, making it a snake, which he transformed back again into a staff? And through that very staff which had been transformed, he changed the water of the Nile into blood, which he also transformed back again into water. Moreover, by an inbreathing of breath he transformed the human being, who was dust, into flesh, and transformed him back again into dust. And was not Moses, though himself flesh, transformed into an exceedingly great light, so that the sons of Israel were unable to look directly at him? Much more, therefore, is God supremely able to transform himself into whatever he wishes.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"περὶ πονηροῦ διαλεγόμενον μὴ αὐτοῦ τοῦ πονηροῦ τὸ θέλημα ποιεῖν","chosen":"discuss evil without doing the will of the evil one himself","rationale":"The first πονηροῦ can denote evil abstractly, while the substantivized αὐτοῦ τοῦ πονηροῦ naturally denotes the evil one; the shift is preserved."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἔχοντες τὰ σώματα τρεπτὰ οὐ τρέπονται","chosen":"since they do not have bodies capable of transformation, do not transform themselves","rationale":"The middle sense maintains the contrast with God’s power to transform himself; “are not transformed” is grammatically possible but conflicts with the following statement that humans are altered over time."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ ἐμφύτου πνεύματος αὐτοῦ ἀπορρήτῳ δυνάμει","chosen":"through his innate spirit and by an ineffable power","rationale":"ἐμφύτου means inborn or inherent, while ἀπόρρητος here describes a power beyond disclosure or expression."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ταύτῃ μᾶλλον ἔστι πιστεῦσαι, ἢ καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ","chosen":"And this is more readily believable than even that the air","rationale":"This retains the comparative force of μᾶλλον ... ἤ. An idiomatic alternative is “This is all the more believable, since even the air,” treating ἤ more loosely as introducing supporting evidence."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ αὐτὸν διήκοντος ἀσωμάτου νοῦ","chosen":"by the incorporeal mind that permeates it","rationale":"διήκοντος depicts the mind as extending through or permeating the air."},{"source_quote":"εἰς μέγιστον ἐτράπη φῶς","chosen":"was transformed into an exceedingly great light","rationale":"The wording presents an actual transformation into light rather than merely describing Moses’s face as shining."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"λίθοι.δὲ","issue":"The printed period and absent following space interrupt a continuing coordinated clause. The sense remains clear as an editorial punctuation or spacing defect.","proposed_reading":"λίθοι δὲ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.7","text":"“But perhaps one of you has considered that one thing can be made into something by another, whereas someone cannot himself transform himself into whatever he wishes, and that being transformed belongs to what grows old and has ..... to die. But one must not think this about immortal beings. For were not ageless angels, ...... and of fiery substance, transformed into flesh? And were not those ...........-ed in Abraham’s presence among them, whose feet men washed as the feet of men of the same substance? Moreover, an angel wrestled with Jacob, who was a human being, after being transformed into flesh so that he could come into bodily contact with him. After wrestling evenly with him, when the angel wished, he was transformed back into his own nature. Then, changing into fire, he did not burn Jacob’s broad sinew, but scorched it and made him lame.

“Now whoever cannot become something else whenever he wishes is mortal, since he is subject to his own nature. But whoever is able to become whatever he wishes whenever he wishes, since he is master of nature itself and returns to youth, is immortal. Therefore, much more does the power of God transform the substance of the body into whatever it wishes whenever it wishes, and by a transformation not previously present it brings forth something of the same substance, though not equal in power. For the one who brings it forth can also turn back toward himself what has been transformed into another substance, whereas the one brought forth, being both a transformation derived from him and his child, cannot become anything else without the will of the one who brought him forth, unless that one wishes it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἄλλος μὲν ὑπ’ ἄλλου γενέσθαι τι δύναται","chosen":"one thing can be made into something by another","rationale":"The masculine ἄλλος may refer to a person, but the argument concerns an entity being transformed by an external agent; “one person” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ὁμοουσίων ἀνθρώπων","chosen":"as the feet of men of the same substance","rationale":"ὁμοούσιος is rendered compositionally to preserve the author’s claim of shared substance without importing later creedal terminology."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα αὐτῷ συγχρωτισθῆναι δυνηθῇ","chosen":"so that he could come into bodily contact with him","rationale":"The rare verb denotes close physical contact, which the wrestling context specifies; “grapple with him” is a viable contextual alternative."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμοούσιον μὴ παρούσῃ τροπῇ προβάλλει, ἰσοδύναμον δὲ οὔ","chosen":"and by a transformation not previously present it brings forth something of the same substance, though not equal in power","rationale":"μὴ παρούσῃ is taken with τροπῇ and understood temporally. It could instead mean “by a transformation that is not present,” but that gives a less intelligible contrast."},{"source_quote":"ὁ μὲν προβάλλων καὶ εἰς ἑτέραν πάλιν οὐσίαν ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν τραπέντα δύναται","chosen":"the one who brings it forth can also turn back toward himself what has been transformed into another substance","rationale":"δύναται is understood with an elliptical causative action supplied from the transformation language. Alternatively, ἐφ’ ἑαυτόν may mean “on his own authority,” but the accusative τραπέντα favors an implied object."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐξ ἐκείνου τροπῆς τε καὶ τέκνον ὑπάρχων","chosen":"being both a transformation derived from him and his child","rationale":"The construction identifies the projected being both as a transformation originating from the projector and as his offspring."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ἀποθανεῖν ..... ἔχοντος","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna between ἀποθανεῖν and ἔχοντος. Its content is unavailable, so the five dots are retained and no restoration is supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἄγγελοι ἀγήρως ...... καὶ πυρώδους οὐσίας","issue":"The selected edition prints a six-dot lacuna after ἀγήρως. The missing wording is not restored; the surviving coordination remains represented around the six dots.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"οἱ παρὰ τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ........... σθέντες","issue":"The selected edition prints an eleven-dot lacuna before the surviving participial fragment σθέντες. The translation preserves the gap and represents σθέντες only as a passive participial ending; no lexical stem is conjectured.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.8","text":"When Peter had said these things, Micaiah, who was himself one of the companions following him, said, “I too would like to learn from you whether, just as the evil one came into being, so also the good one came into being. If they came into being in the same way, they seem to me to be brothers.”

Peter replied, “They did not come into being in the same way, if indeed you remember what I said at the beginning: that the fourfold substance of the evil one’s body, having been carefully separated by God, was brought forth; but when substance outside it had been mixed for the mixture in accordance with the will of the one who brought it forth, the disposition that delights in evils arose. Thus one should understand that the fourfold substance brought forth from God is God’s child and itself exists eternally, whereas the disposition that delights in evils, which occurred contingently in the substance mixed externally by him, supervened. Thus it was neither begotten by God nor by anyone else; neither was it brought forth by him, nor did it come forth spontaneously, nor did it always exist, as the substance did before the commingling. Rather, in accordance with God’s will, it occurred contingently in the external mixture. We have said many times that this must be so.

“But the good one, having been begotten from God’s most beautiful transformation and not having occurred contingently through an external mixture, is truly a son. Nevertheless, since these things are unwritten and have been made credible by conjectures, let the ....... not be confirmed as certainly being so. If not, the mind, as though it had certainly grasped ...........es, ceases searching. And remember those instructions of mine too: such things .......n must not be spoken, but only to those who have proved most trustworthy after testing. Nor should such things be asserted lightly even among yourselves, and you ought not dare to speak as though you had precisely established the discovery of secret things. Rather, you should remain silent and only ponder them. For in speaking, the one who utters them may perhaps sin by not speaking as the matter stands, and will incur punishment for having dared—even to himself—to utter things honored by silence.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ πονηρὸς ... ὁ ἀγαθός","chosen":"the evil one ... the good one","rationale":"Both adjectives are substantivized masculine singulars and refer to personal beings within the argument, not merely to abstract evil and good."},{"source_quote":"ἡ τετραγενὴς τοῦ σώματος οὐσία","chosen":"the fourfold substance of the ... body","rationale":"τετραγενής describes a substance constituted in fourfold fashion; “four-element substance” is possible if the author’s cosmological elements are made explicit."},{"source_quote":"πεφιλοκρινημένη ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ","chosen":"having been carefully separated by God","rationale":"φιλοκρινέω denotes discriminating or separating accurately. “Carefully selected” is possible, but the subsequent mixture language favors separation."},{"source_quote":"ἡ συμβεβηκυῖα κακοῖς χαίρουσα προαίρεσις ἐπεγένετο","chosen":"the disposition that delights in evils, which occurred contingently ... supervened","rationale":"The rendering preserves both συμβεβηκυῖα, with its sense of an accidental or contingent occurrence, and ἐπεγένετο, which marks a subsequent arising."},{"source_quote":"οὔτε ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ προβέβληται","chosen":"neither was it brought forth by him","rationale":"αὐτοῦ most immediately refers to the previously mentioned agent involved in projection, but whether the referent is God or the evil one is not fully explicit; “by him” preserves that ambiguity."},{"source_quote":"στοχασμοῖς πεπιστωμένα","chosen":"have been made credible by conjectures","rationale":"στοχασμοί are reasoned conjectures or inferences rather than certain demonstrations."},{"source_quote":"τὰ σιγῇ τετιμημένα","chosen":"things honored by silence","rationale":"The personified expression treats silence as the proper honor accorded to secret matters."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μὴ πάντως ἡ ....... οὕτως ἔχειν βεβαιούσθω","issue":"The selected edition prints a seven-dot lacuna after the article ἡ. The missing feminine subject cannot be recovered from the supplied text, so the gap is retained without restoration.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁ νοῦς ὡς πάντως προειληφὼς ........... ες τοῦ ζητεῖν παύεται","issue":"The selected edition prints an eleven-dot lacuna followed by the surviving fragment ες. Because the fragment has no independently recoverable lexical meaning, it is represented as the ending “es” after the eleven dots; no complete word is conjectured.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅτι τὰ τοιαῦτα .......ν οὐ δεῖ λέγειν","issue":"The selected edition prints a seven-dot lacuna before the surviving final ν. The damaged expression is retained as seven dots plus an English-letter representation of the ending, without supplying a missing word or syntactic function.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.9","text":"When Peter had said these things, a certain Lazarus, himself one of the followers, said, “Tell us how the reconciliation is possible: how can it be reasonable for the evil one, who was appointed by a righteous God to be the punisher of those who acted impiously, later to be sent with his angels and the sinners into the lower darkness? For I remember that the Teacher himself said this too.”

Peter said, “I too acknowledge that the evil one does nothing evil in this respect, insofar as he carries out the law given to him. Although he has an evil disposition, nevertheless, because of his fear of God, he does nothing unjustly. But because he slanders teachers of truth in order to ensnare the undiscerning, this same being is also called the Slanderer.

“As for our truthful Teacher’s saying that he and his angels would depart with the deceived sinners into the lower darkness, it has an explanation like this. The evil one, having been allotted a constitution that delights in darkness, descends with his fellow-servant angels into the darkness of Tartarus and takes pleasure in it, for darkness is congenial to fire. But human souls, being drops of pure light, are drunk in together by a substance of alien fire; and since they do not have a nature capable of dying, they are punished according to their deserts.

“But if the ruler of wickedness, being a human being, is not sent into the darkness because he does not delight in it, then his constitution that delights in evils can be recombined into a disposition toward good, and thus, as good, he will be judged to live in fellowship. This is all the more so because, although he had been allotted a constitution that delights in evils, on account of his fear of God he did nothing contrary to what seemed right to God’s law. Surely, then, by the high priest Aaron’s staff becoming a snake and being transformed back again into a staff, Scripture mystically foreshadowed this: the recombination of the evil one’s transformation that will take place later and is yet to be.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Τὴν συμφωνίαν ἡμῖν εἰπὲ","chosen":"Tell us how the reconciliation is possible","rationale":"συμφωνία denotes agreement or consistency; here Lazarus asks how two apparently conflicting claims can be reconciled. “Explain the consistency to us” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"διαβάλλων δὲ διδασκάλους ἀληθείας ... καὶ διάβολος ὁ αὐτὸς ὀνομάζεται","chosen":"because he slanders teachers of truth ... this same being is also called the Slanderer","rationale":"Rendering both διαβάλλων and διάβολος with the same word family preserves the explicit etymological association; “the Devil” would preserve the conventional title but obscure that association."},{"source_quote":"σκότῳ χαίρουσαν τὴν κρᾶσιν λελογχώς","chosen":"having been allotted a constitution that delights in darkness","rationale":"κρᾶσις literally denotes a mixture, but here refers to the being’s composite constitution. “Mixture” remains a more formal alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ ἀλλοφύλου πυρὸς οὐσίας συμπινόμεναι","chosen":"are drunk in together by a substance of alien fire","rationale":"The passive participle from συμπίνω retains the image of the soul-drops being drunk or swallowed in together. Renderings such as “compressed” are smoother but are not directly supported by this verb."},{"source_quote":"μετασυγκριθῆναι εἰς ἀγαθοῦ προαίρεσιν","chosen":"be recombined into a disposition toward good","rationale":"μετασυγκρίνω describes a renewed or altered combination, continuing the author’s mixture terminology; ἀγαθοῦ is taken objectively as the good toward which the disposition is directed."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὕτως ἀγαθὸς συνεῖναι κριθήσεται","chosen":"and thus, as good, he will be judged to live in fellowship","rationale":"ἀγαθός is treated as a predicate describing the subject, while συνεῖναι means to be or live together. The text does not explicitly state with whom he would live, so no complement is added."},{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ πονηροῦ ὕστερον γενησομένην τῆς τροπῆς μετασύγκρισιν ... ἐσομένην","chosen":"the recombination of the evil one’s transformation that will take place later and is yet to be","rationale":"Both future expressions are represented rather than silently removing the source’s apparent repetition."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὴν τοῦ πονηροῦ ὕστερον γενησομένην τῆς τροπῆς μετασύγκρισιν μυστηριωδῶς ἡ γραφὴ ἐσομένην προεδήλωσε","issue":"Both γενησομένην and ἐσομένην appear to modify the feminine μετασύγκρισιν, producing a redundant and syntactically awkward pair of future expressions. The confirmed printed wording is retained rather than emended.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.10","text":"After Lazarus, Joseph—himself also one of the followers—said, “You have said..... everything correctly. Grant me this also, since I wish to learn: why is it that, for everyone, from the same words ......... some are persuaded, while others refuse to believe?”

Peter said, “The words are not incantations, so that anyone who hears must necessarily believe. Rather, the fact that some are persuaded and others are not intelligently demonstrates freedom of choice.”

When he had said these things, we all blessed him.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ λόγοι ἐπῳδαί","chosen":"the words are not incantations","rationale":"ἐπῳδαί are charms or magical spells intended to compel an effect; “incantations” suits the contrast with freely given belief."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα πάντως ἀκούσας τις πιστεύσῃ","chosen":"so that anyone who hears must necessarily believe","rationale":"πάντως gives the sense of an inevitable result, not merely a strong likelihood."},{"source_quote":"συνετῶς δείκνυται τὸ αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"intelligently demonstrates freedom of choice","rationale":"αὐτεξούσιον denotes self-determination or freedom of agency. συνετῶς may alternatively be rendered “reasonably” or “clearly.”"},{"source_quote":"οἱ μὲν πείθονται, οἱ δὲ ἀπειθοῦσι","chosen":"some are persuaded, while others refuse to believe","rationale":"The rendering preserves the contrast between responding to persuasion and resisting or disobeying it."},{"source_quote":"οἱ πάντες εὐλογήσαμεν","chosen":"we all blessed him","rationale":"εὐλογέω can mean bless, praise, or speak well of. “Blessed” preserves the formal wording, with Peter understood as the object from the preceding participial construction."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"Ὀρθῶς πάντα εἴρ.....","issue":"The selected edition prints a five-dot lacuna after the surviving verbal beginning εἴρ. The translation represents the recognizable saying-verb followed by the five dots, but supplies no missing Greek ending.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"διὰ τί πᾶσι τῶν αὐτῶν λόγων ......... οἱ μὲν πείθονται","issue":"The selected edition prints a nine-dot lacuna between λόγων and οἱ. The surviving syntax is incomplete, so the translation remains correspondingly damaged and does not restore a verb or participle within the gap.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
